statements: Header compatibility with the Slice 1 library is complete for this revision: the catalog admitted all 79 headers under strict tiling, the index and the headers agree in both directions, and mlx-affine classified all 1401 module paths with zero refusals under the Slice 1 resolution rules. This is NOT Q0 payload identity and NOT numerical qualification.

The conversion quantized routed experts at the configuration default (4-bit, group 64) and every other quantized module at an explicit 8-bit, group-64 override; all 704 overrides resolve to a quantized module whose stored shapes agree with 8 bits. No override is `False`, redundant with the default, or unresolved.

Only two quantization combinations occur, 4/64/BF16 (225 modules) and 8/64/BF16 (704 modules), and both lie inside Slice 1's admitted domain (bits {4,8}, group {32,64,128}, metadata {F16,BF16,F32}). The F16 and F32 metadata paths are not exercised by this checkpoint.

Routed-expert weights are stacked with a leading expert dimension E=256 for layers 3-77 (switch_mlp gate/up: weight [256,2048,768], scales/biases [256,2048,96]; down: weight [256,6144,256], scales/biases [256,6144,32]). They carry 95.3% of tensor bytes. Slice 1's slicing arithmetic accepts these shapes: the last expert plane of all 381 stacked triples (225 expert, 156 per-head MLA) ends exactly at its tensor's end. That is arithmetic over metadata, not a payload read.
MLA's absorbed per-head projections embed_q [64,512,in 192] and unembed_out [64,256,in 512] are stored as 8-bit triples with a leading head dimension of 64, in every layer 0-77.

The indexer is present only in the 21 layers the configuration lists as `full` (0-2 and every fourth layer from 6 to 74) and is entirely unquantized BF16, including wq_b [4096,2048], wk [128,6144] and weights_proj [32,6144]. The `shared` layers carry no indexer tensors.

No next-token-prediction (MTP) tensors are present although config reports num_nextn_predict_layers 1: layer indices stop at 77 of num_hidden_layers 78. This MLX conversion therefore cannot supply an MTP head.

The index's metadata.total_size equals the sum of whole shard file sizes (tensor bytes plus every 8-byte prefix and header), not the sum of tensor bytes; the difference is exactly the 411,576 header bytes. The writer evidently counted file sizes. A check that equated total_size with tensor bytes would refuse this checkpoint.

Shard sizes recorded at download time equal today's stat sizes for all 79 shards, and the download record says every file was verified at download (2026-09-22). This census did not re-hash anything; the per-shard sha256 values it carries are the record's, not re-verified.

The repository ships model code (glm_moe_dsa.py, named by config model_file) and a compiled upstream __pycache__/glm_moe_dsa.cpython-314.pyc (41,195 bytes) that the download record lists as an upstream file. Both were listed, neither was read, imported or executed. A loader must never execute either.
